final_state.note: policy_accepted_at/customer_consents_count show as null/0 in the qa_turn_helper state snapshot despite the customers table row showing policy_accepted_at set — this is a known state-command-vs-DB reconciliation artifact documented in prior QA runs (Fase E), not a new bug introduced by this scenario.

langfuse_pull_error: 401 Unauthorized — Invalid Langfuse credentials (known issue, credential regeneration pending per project runbook)

observations.hook_1_escalation_during_indecision: NOT TRIGGERED. Across all 11 turns (3 service pivots, 3 date changes, 1 explicitly ambiguous message), the bot never called the escalate/send_to_human tool and never handed off to a human. The previously-fixed 'escalate after 2 consecutive date rejections' bug did NOT reproduce, even though this scenario intentionally rejected the date twice in a row (viernes->sábado in turn 5, then sábado->viernes in turn 7).
observations.hook_2_final_intent_match: MATCH. The booked appointment (id 1fce4177-7b86-4a79-a0a6-2fbd1fcae2d0) is corte + tinte (service_names: Tinte, Corte de Mujer), Friday 2026-07-10 15:20-16:40 (afternoon), stylist Marta (resolved from no_preference_stylist=true / 'any stylist'). This exactly matches the LAST stated intent, not the discarded corte-only, tinte-only, or Saturday intents.
observations.hook_3_ambiguous_message_handling: GOOD. On 'buff no sé, lo que sea' (turn 6, in response to a stylist-preference question), the bot did not stall or ask a vague follow-up — it resolved the ambiguity into a concrete decision (no_preference_stylist=true, 'la primera con disponibilidad') and moved the flow forward to the next required field (customer name). Same pattern later for the vague 'por la tarde' preference: the bot proposed 3 concrete time options (14:00, 15:20, 16:40) rather than guessing or looping.
observations.hook_4_draft_mutation_evidence: CORRECT. Every pivot (corte->tinte in turn 2, corte->corte+tinte in turn 3, viernes->sábado in turn 5, sábado->viernes in turn 7) is reflected as an update_booking tool call that overwrites the relevant single field in place (services, date_iso) rather than appending or creating a second draft/appointment. Only one book() call occurred at the very end (turn 11), producing exactly one appointment row (appt_count_delta: 1). No duplicate or orphan appointments were created.
observations.hook_5_turn_count: 11 user turns to completion — within the ~14-turn budget, no flag needed.
